title: Molecular basis of single-mismatch-induced nuclease-to-nickase conversion in TIGR-TasH.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded both deposited structures as mmCIF text files from RCSB: 25QK (TasH-tigRNA-MM1 dsDNA complex, 0.80 MB, 6,803 atom records, 3.04 A resolution) and 25QL (MM5 complex, 0.61 MB, 5,153 atom records, 3.02 A). Both parsed cleanly and their primary citation field matches this paper's DOI. Confirmed the matching cryo-EM map entry EMD-80301 is released in the Electron Microscopy Data Bank via its application programming interface. Confirmed the text-mined IDs 9W03/9W04 belong to a different, companion Molecular Cell paper, not this one.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biochemical results (which mismatch positions convert the enzyme from a double-strand cutter to a single-strand nicker, gel-based cleavage assays, mutant activity) are described in figures only; no numeric table was retrievable. Europe PMC's supplementary-file listing timed out on two attempts, so the supplement contents are unknown (recorded as not retrievable).

a1_downloadable.note: Both structure files and the map entry are public and downloaded without login; total 1.4 MB.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL and stop. There is no label column anywhere in the released data. The only deposited data are two atomic coordinate files and two density maps; the quantity of interest (does a given mismatch position give a double-strand cut or a single-strand nick, and how efficiently) exists only as gel images inside figures and would have to be constructed by eye from those images.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Two structures, two maps. Even if every gel lane in the paper were digitised, the design covers roughly five mismatch positions plus a handful of protein mutants, i.e. tens of measurements, far under the ~400 minimum.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed beyond noting the guide RNA and target DNA sequences are present inside the two mmCIF files; project already dead at A2/A5.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed; no measurement table exists to carry units. Dead at A2/A5.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 1.4 MB of mmCIF; maps would add a few hundred MB if needed

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The two PDB IDs and two map IDs named in the data availability statement all resolve and match; nothing else to count.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed; there is no label. Dead at A2/A5.

integration.partner_dataset: Protein Data Bank / Electron Microscopy Data Bank entries for the related TIGR-Tas structures (9W03, 9W04, 9W26) from the companion Molecular Cell paper, joinable on PDB ID.
integration.join_key: PDB ID / UniProt-style protein identity of TasH
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Even pooled, the whole TIGR-Tas structural literature amounts to a handful of structures, so no joined dataset reaches modelling scale.

controls.positive_control: None definable without a measurement table.
controls.external_validation: None; no second source measures mismatch tolerance for TIGR-Tas.

honest_claim_h3: No model could be trained from this paper's released data; the only honest claim available is a structural description of two mismatch-bound complexes.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use guide-RNA and target-DNA sequence pairs to predict whether a single mismatch gives a full cut or only a nick.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model a guide RNA paired with a DNA target carrying one mismatch at a known position. This paper supplies two such pairs as atomic structures and roughly five more as gel lanes in figures; verified count of modellable examples is 2.
plain_idea.predict: Cutting outcome at each mismatch position: double-strand break, single-strand nick, or no cut. Truth would come from gel-based cleavage assays run by hand, which exist only as figure images here, not as numbers.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Genome-editing groups adopting the new TIGR-Tas enzymes would want a guide-design rule for mismatch tolerance, as exists for CRISPR-Cas9. But that needs a high-throughput mismatch screen, which this paper does not contain.

more_or_better_data.why: Cas9 off-target predictors such as R-CRISPR and CCLMoff were trained on tens of thousands of guide-target pairs from high-throughput screens; this paper offers two structures and a handful of gel lanes.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurement values are released, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be estimated from this data.

models_beatable.why: Irrelevant here: the existing models cover Cas9, a different enzyme family, and we have no TIGR-Tas training data with which to compete or compare.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: there is no training table, so no baseline can be run on a shared split.

ml_idea: The attractive idea would be a guide-design model for TIGR-Tas enzymes: predict, from a dual-spacer guide RNA and its DNA target, whether a mismatch at each position yields a double-strand cut, a nick, or nothing, the way CRISPR-Cas9 off-target predictors do. This paper cannot support it. Its released data are two cryo-EM structures (PDB 25QK and 25QL, which I downloaded and parsed) plus two density maps, and the cleavage outcomes live only in gel images. The project would need a high-throughput mismatch library screen on TasH, which nobody has published yet; if such a screen appears, revisit using these two structures as mechanistic features rather than as training data.

effort.compute_note: Measured file sizes directly: 0.80 MB and 0.61 MB of mmCIF text, trivial to load. No cross-validation is possible because there is no labelled table, so timing estimates are null rather than guessed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled rows in the data availability statement's deposits. It took one minute: two structures and two maps, no measurement table. That kills it.

verdict_reason: Structural biology paper whose entire released dataset is two cryo-EM structures and two maps (both downloaded and verified). Fails A2 because the outcome of interest, cut versus nick, exists only as gel images in figures, and fails A5 with two examples against a ~400 minimum.
